subject: Clarifying DPA roles, PII routing and breach notification playbook
messages:
From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@medsync.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 07 Sep 2026 14:02:00 -0700
Subject: Quick recap and outstanding privacy asks from today

Alex — thanks for the call this morning, appreciate the clarity on your integration patterns. Quick recap and the asks we promised to follow up on: 

1) PII routing: you described sending hashed patient IDs and free-text clinical notes to Redwood for feature generation. We flagged two modes — transient inference-only processing vs. storage for retraining. Please confirm you only want transient handling for now (no model training).

2) Data residency & logs: you asked whether request logs with IPs and timestamps are retained and where they live. Short answer: request logs are stored in the US by default; we can offer EU residency for enterprises. Retention defaults to 90 days; we can configure longer retention for auditable accounts.

3) Subprocessors & breach notice: you asked about subprocessors list and our notify timeline. I've attached the latest DPA draft (DPA_MedSync_Draft_v2.pdf) and an evidence matrix. We will confirm the subprocessor roster and the exact breach-notification SLA we can commit to in writing.

Next steps (from Redwood):
- We’ll send an annotated DPA with clarifying language around controller/processor mapping and a short appendix on PII routing options (action: Marissa to draft).
- Vivek to surface technical logs retention options and a sample logging policy for your SOC/Ops team.
- Neha will propose a breach-notify timeline we can reasonably commit to and list any required customer-side obligations for triage.

Can you confirm if the transient-only data flow is acceptable for the pilot? If so we’ll mark training/storage sections as out-of-scope and iterate the DPA accordingly.

Thanks — Sergio

--
Sergio Alvarez
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
sergio.alvarez@redwoodinference.com
+1 (415) 555-0199
From: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@medsync.com>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Customer Success <customersuccess@medsync.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 07 Sep 2026 16:09:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Quick recap and outstanding privacy asks from today

Thanks Sergio — that matches our notes. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Pilot is transient-only; we will not allow training on patient data during the pilot. Good to mark training/storage out-of-scope for now.
- Logs: we need access to request-level logs (no patient content) for 180 days for a limited audit team. IPs and timestamps suffice; we do not require request bodies.
- Breach notify: our legal team expects a 24-hour initial notification (email + secure portal) if Redwood determines an incident impacts MedSync data, followed by a 72-hour preliminary incident report. We understand this may require review, but want to flag it as a requirement if we proceed with a pilot that touches PHI.

Attaching the internal list of auditors as: auditors@medsync.com (we'll loop them when you have the evidence matrix).

Alex
Director, Integrations — MedSync Health
alex.johnson@medsync.com
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@medsync.com>
Cc: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwoodinference.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 08 Sep 2026 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Quick recap and outstanding privacy asks from today

Alex — thanks for the confirmation. A couple of legal/contract items we’ll propose based on your asks: 

1) Controller vs. Processor: we propose language that keeps MedSync as Controller for patient data; Redwood will be Processor for transient inference operations. We will add a short definition for "transient processing" (no storage beyond ephemeral inference cache, no training, no reuse).

2) Log retention & scope: we can increase log retention to 180 days for request metadata (IP, timestamp, request id) per your audit requirement. We will explicitly exclude request/response bodies from the log snapshot provided to auditors unless you ask otherwise and sign an addendum.

3) Breach notification timing: Redwood’s standard is "reasonable efforts" to notify within 72 hours for confirmed incidents. For customers handling PHI we can offer a specific SLA for initial notification within 24 hours for incidents classified by Redwood as "impacting customer data" — provided the incident meets Redwood’s internal triage threshold and you accept limited conditions around what constitutes an "impacting" incident (we'll add examples in the DPA).

4) Subprocessors: we’ll attach a current subprocessors list and a monthly notification cadence for additions; we will provide an escalation path if you require prior approval for certain categories (e.g., analytics providers).

I'm attaching an annotated DPA (see DPA_MedSync_Draft_v2.pdf) with tracked changes for the controller/processor paragraph and a new section on log retention. Sergio/Vivek — please review the proposed 24-hour initial notification SLA and confirm operational feasibility.

Best,
Marissa
Head of Legal Operations, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com
From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
To: auditors@medsync.com, Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@medsync.com>
Cc: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 09 Sep 2026 09:21:00 -0700
Subject: Evidence matrix and operational steps — next actions

Hi Alex + MedSync audit team — following the thread, attaching the operational evidence matrix (redwood-evidence-matrix.xlsx) that maps controls to artifacts we can produce for your SOC/Ops review. Highlights: 

- Logs: we will provide exported request metadata (IP, timestamp, request id) on a secure Share link for a 180-day window. Exports will contain no request/response bodies unless explicitly requested via the addendum.
- Breach playbook: attached is a short-runbook describing Redwood's incident classification and notification flow; we propose a 24-hour initial notification for "impacting customer data" incidents with a 72-hour preliminary report to follow. The playbook includes the internal steps we take and the customer obligations for triage.
- Subprocessors: current roster is included in the DPA appendix; additions will be sent monthly and we can mark categories that require prior review.

Next actions (we'd like confirmation by EOD next Tue):
- MedSync to confirm transient-only pilot scope and provide the auditors distribution list.
- MedSync legal to indicate whether the 24-hour initial notification SLA is acceptable as written (Marissa has flagged the limited carveouts).
- Redwood to provide a signed addendum with the updated log-retention term and the evidence export process.

Attachment stubs: DPA_MedSync_Draft_v2.pdf (PDF) — annotated; redwood-evidence-matrix.xlsx (XLSX) — control mapping

If helpful, Vivek can run a short technical walkthrough next week showing the export and redaction flow.

Thanks — Neha
Privacy & Trust, Redwood Inference
